analyst_view.overall: Hoffenheim (23rd, 4 pts) host Sturm Graz (24th, 4 pts) in a game both need to stay in the play-off race, with coach Christian Ilzer, who won the double with Sturm in 2024, facing his old club and saying Hoffenheim will try everything to win. Hoffenheim lost 1-0 at Frankfurt on Saturday and drew 1-1 with Crystal Palace last time in Europe; Gendrey, Hajdari, Hranac and De Cat are out (all counted) and Wimmer (hamstring) also missed the weekend, while Ozan Kabak, banned in the Bundesliga, is expected to start in Europe according to two previews. Sturm are six games without a win, lost 3-2 at home to Celje last time in Europe, and miss Grgic, Khudyakov, Kiteishvili and Rozga (all counted), with Koller doubtful through illness. Portuguese referee Luis Godinho (about 4.5 cards a game) is in charge; with nothing the numbers cannot see, every stat stays where they put it. A squad page this evening lists Kabak as banned and Wimmer, Prass and Conte as doubts; the Kabak ban is his Bundesliga one per the two previews, and the doubts are not confirmed, so nothing moves.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (Hoffenheim 2.1) and already include Hoffenheim's recent form and the absences on both lists. Kabak's expected start keeps Hoffenheim's defence as usual, Wimmer's absence was already there at the weekend, and Sturm's slump is in their recent results, so I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, mostly Hoffenheim (7.2), already up a little for Sturm winning corners lately. Hoffenheim should have most of the ball at home against a Sturm side likely to defend in a back three, which the split already shows, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already up about 11% for Hoffenheim drawing many bookings lately and about 5% for referee Luis Godinho (4.5 a game). Ilzer's reunion with his old club and several thousand Sturm fans add atmosphere but no sign of bad blood, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.1 shots, already up about 12% for Hoffenheim's busy recent shooting (103 in six). Kramaric and Lemperle are expected to start, which is the attack those recent games already show, so I stay at 32.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, already a little lower for Sturm's recent finishing. Hoffenheim's attack has no new absences and Sturm's injured players are all counted, so I stay at 9.7.
